description:
Get one gallery chart by slug: what it shows, the data it needs, sample data, and the exact runnable POST /api/v1/render request. Optionally render it in the same call. The look is written into the request's theme, so no saved brand kit is needed.

Use this tool when: list_gallery_charts showed a chart that fits and you want its request body, or want it rendered with your own data.
Modes: render "none" (default) returns the description, data shape, sample data and the request JSON. Change data.labels, every datasets[].data, and then header and kpiStrip (they hold numbers too) so they all agree, then call render_card, or call this tool again with render "image" or "url" and overrides. Overrides are a shallow merge: a top-level key you give replaces that key in the request completely.
This is a gallery chart, not a template id for /api/v1/templates.
Behavior: render "image" or "url" makes a Chart-Output API call and uses a render. If your plan's size limit is smaller than the chart at 2x, it is retried once at 1x and the result says so.

Returns: text (and the image for render "image").
Errors (the message is plain text and keeps the API's details): 400 — invalid spec; every failing field is listed with its path. 401 — API key missing or invalid. 402 — monthly allowance used up; do NOT retry, tell the user (the message has the reset date and an upgrade link). 403 — the plan does not include something you used (pdf, a size above the plan cap, a brand kit over the limit); do NOT retry the same request, tell the user. 404 — unknown brand slug (the message lists the available ones). 429 — rate-limited; wait for Retry-After. Network error — chart-output.com is unreachable or timed out.
Errors specific to this tool: unknown slug — "No gallery chart named X"; call list_gallery_charts.

overrides.description: Top-level request fields that replace the same fields in the gallery request, e.g. {data: {...}, header: {...}, kpiStrip: [...]}.

render.description: "none" (default) returns the request JSON only. "image" renders it inline. "url" renders it and returns a link.

slug.description: Gallery slug from list_gallery_charts, for example "mrr-growth".

name: get_gallery_chart
